subject.title: fix(heartbeat): stop reporting success after tool failures

question: Should `observeToolTerminal` become the shared host-owned terminal-outcome contract for embedded, Codex, and Copilot attempts?
rationale: The implementation is coherent and proven, but it expands a plugin-facing harness contract and changes cross-runtime failure precedence, which requires explicit owner acceptance rather than automation inference.

options.title: Approve the shared host contract
options.body: Accept the optional observer as the canonical cross-runtime boundary and land after rebasing and required checks complete.

options.title: Narrow the first landing
options.body: Limit the fix to the heartbeat and Codex path, accepting temporary sibling divergence and a follow-up for Copilot and generic embedded behavior.

options.title: Pause the contract expansion
options.body: Keep the PR open while maintainers choose a different terminal-outcome API or ownership boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve the shared host contract
recommendation.body: Accept the optional observer as the canonical cross-runtime boundary and land after rebasing and required checks complete.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the broadest repeated integration work across heartbeat delivery and runtime behavior in the central runner.
